title: Radios, mixers and modulation
blurb: Explain what a transceiver, mixer, oscillator, VFO and transverter do, and the difference between sensitivity and selectivity.

T7A01.why: **Sensitivity** is how weak a signal the receiver can still detect.
T7A01.trap: Selectivity is about separating signals, not detecting faint ones. RF gain is just a control.

T7A02.trap: Matching to 50 ohms is a tuner's job; converting bands is a transverter's.

T7A03.why: A **mixer** combines two frequencies and so shifts a signal to another frequency.
T7A03.trap: An amplifier makes a signal bigger, not different in frequency.

T7A04.why: **Selectivity** is how well a receiver picks one signal out from several nearby ones.
T7A04.trap: Sensitivity is about weak signals, not crowded ones.

T7A05.why: An **oscillator** generates a signal at a specific frequency.
T7A05.trap: Filters shape signals and modulators add information. Neither creates the frequency.

T7A06.why: A **transverter** converts a radio's input and output to another band.
T7A06.trap: Filters only block frequencies; they don't move a signal to another band.

T7A07.why: Grounding the **PTT** (push-to-talk) input flips the transceiver from receive to transmit.
T7A07.trap: PTT isn't a CW key input or a tuning tone.

T7A08.why: **Modulation** is combining speech (the information) with an RF carrier so it can travel as a radio wave.
T7A08.trap: Oscillation makes the carrier; modulation is what puts the voice on it.

T7A09.why: The SSB or CW-FM switch sets the amplifier for **proper operation in that mode**. It doesn't change your signal or the band.

T7A10.why: An **RF power amplifier** on the transceiver's output raises transmitted power.
T7A10.trap: A potentiometer is a variable resistor; it only reduces signals.

T7A11.why: The **VFO** is the tuning oscillator: it sets the receive and transmit frequency.
T7A11.trap: Generating and demodulating SSB is done by other circuits.
